first_step_test: One long diagonal handle joined to one short rake-head bar gives the learner a useful connected tool silhouette in its final position before the tines and leaf pile arrive.

source.notes: Planned six-panel direct felt-tip marker contact sheet for the September 11 current lesson. Early autumn supplies a natural seasonal hook; the rake-and-pile overlap is distinct from recent object, animal, and food lessons. Preserve rejected iterations privately.

frames.visible_job: Draw one long rounded handle on a diagonal and attach one short rake-head bar across its lower-right end.
frames.instruction: Ghost a diagonal from upper left to lower right twice, then draw the rounded wooden handle in one confident pass. Attach one short bar across its lower-right tip so the tool already points into the future pile.

frames.visible_job: Attach exactly five evenly spaced curved tines to the lower edge of the rake-head bar.
frames.instruction: From the lower edge of the rake-head bar, pull exactly five short curved tines downward. Space their roots evenly, keep every tip visible, and compare the four narrow gaps before moving on.

frames.visible_job: Draw one low scalloped leaf-pile silhouette behind the rake tips without covering any tine.
frames.instruction: Begin left of the rake head and build one low scalloped mound across the bottom of the page. Route its upper edge behind the five visible tine tips, then close the pile with a shallow lower curve.

frames.visible_job: Add exactly five distinct leaf shapes across and above the pile while keeping the rake silhouette clear.
frames.instruction: Add exactly five leaves: a five-point leaf at left, an oval near the upper-left edge, a three-lobed leaf below the rake head, a narrow leaf at right, and one small five-point leaf floating above the pile. Keep each silhouette separate enough to color cleanly.

frames.visible_job: Draw two short wind curls around the floating leaf and one broken ground shadow beneath the pile.
frames.instruction: Curve one short breeze mark on each side of the floating leaf, then draw one broken shadow beneath the pile. Leave small paper gaps in the shadow so it feels quick and handmade.

final_step.visible_job: Add brown, charcoal, orange, yellow, coral, teal, and navy marker fills only inside the established shapes.
final_step.instruction: Color the handle warm brown and the rake head and five tines charcoal. Fill the pile with loose orange and yellow strokes, then color the five established leaves coral, orange, yellow, and teal. Deepen the two breeze curls and existing broken shadow with navy, preserve paper streaks, and add no new outlines.
adds: brown charcoal orange yellow coral teal and navy marker fills

visual_review.first_step_observation: The first crop presents one connected diagonal handle and attached head bar at their final scale and angle, giving a beginner a useful tool silhouette without premature tines, leaves, shadow, or color.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: All six saved crops were reviewed at readable size. Each adjacent pair adds only its assigned forms; the handle-to-head joint, five separate tine roots and tips, scalloped pile edge, five distinct leaves, two curls, and broken shadow retain their anchors through the marker-color finish.
